A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoleBench/ReBind study. Their readable main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching renamed and relocated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original image-generation experiments, human preference evaluations, fine-tuning ablations and compositional-generalization results.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds benchmark validation, attention visualizations, SD3 generalization results, COCO evaluation and training-sample ablations.

M1.justification: The active/passive decomposition, DALL-E 3 intermediate generation, β<0 filtering and λ-weighted LoRA objective remain unchanged. FT Inter. is consistently renamed ReBind. Applying the framework to SD3 does not document a new algorithmic component or adaptation.

E1.justification: V3 adds COCO 2017 validation prompts, extending evaluation to general image generation beyond controlled action relations. RoleBench's ten relations, listed triplets, intermediates and existing unseen-object/relation scenarios are retained; expanded construction descriptions do not establish changed RoleBench data.

E2.justification: V3 Table 7 adds pretrained SD3 as a comparator for ReBind in the existing multi-relation generalization experiment; v2 Table 6 compared only SDXL and its fine-tuned variant. Main benchmark comparators and human-study comparator membership remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 adds distinct evaluation protocols: matched SDXL/ReBind generation on 5,000 COCO validation prompts using CLIPScore and FID, SD3 configurations for multi-relation evaluation, and additional training-image counts N=1,3,5,10. Appendix B.2 adds Mistral-7B plausibility and reported search-count validation. Existing RoleBench sampling and role-specific metrics remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine frequency-label validity (Appendix B.2), action-token attention under role reversal (Figure 8), sensitivity to training images per prompt (Table 10), and general-image-quality preservation (Table 8). Existing λ, frequent-composition, unseen-relation/object and reversed-intermediate analyses are retained, including material newly summarized in the main text.

E5.justification: V2 consistently reports seed 42. V3 Section 4 changes the training/ablation seed to 24, while Appendix E still specifies 42, leaving the actual seed unresolved. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests; human-rating correlations are unchanged.

E6.justification: V3 substantially expands reported findings through validation, SD3, COCO and N-sweep results. Its COCO comparison reports SDXL/ReBind CLIPScore 21.17/21.20 and FID 83.95/90.56; new SD3 results include worse similar-relation β after fine-tuning, 0.6 versus 7.6. Most matched earlier scores remain unchanged. Table 2 nevertheless changes R2F spatial Match from 68.7 to 68.0 and SLD's spatial improvement annotation from 5.4 to 5.0 without corresponding β changes.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, role-collapse formulation, directional composition definitions and weighted loss are mathematically unchanged. Explicit image/prompt arguments clarify the existing β definition. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added frequency validation is empirical.

C1.justification: The central RoleBench, role-collapse and intermediate-decomposition contributions remain. V3 softens the abstract's presence-versus-absence explanation by saying frequent counterparts also contribute, and removes v2's unqualified conclusion that improvements maintain image quality.

C2.justification: The central distributional-bias interpretation is retained. V3 adds an attention-based explanation of agent–patient confusion and acknowledges object entanglement, imitation of synthetic training styles and frequent-prompt alignment losses. Its new COCO discussion interprets alignment as preserved despite worse FID, qualifying the earlier image-quality narrative.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents RoleBench candidate sourcing, GPT-4o generation and manual filtering, and states that kissing was excluded from human evaluation and qualitative analysis; the PDFs do not establish that this exclusion began in v3. It adds a project-page link and removes the future code/data-release promise, without establishing actual availability. Most implementation settings and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds semantic-plausibility references by Kauf and Pedinotti, cites Magnet in rare-concept discussion, and adds COCO, CLIPScore and FID references. These support benchmark construction and additional evaluation while preserving the existing research positioning. Preprint-to-publication bibliography updates do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the introduction, problem definition, experimental setup and results narrative, consistently replaces FT Inter. terminology with ReBind, and reorganizes the appendix into lettered sections with construction and validation subsections. It also shortens the title and adds acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V3 reformats Figure 2, enlarges and relocates the main qualitative comparison, and redisplays existing appendix evidence through main-text intermediate and frequent-composition summaries. It adds attention maps, COCO and N-ablation tables, expands the generalization table, and reorganizes numerous figure/table placements and captions.

improvement.justification: V3 improves assessability through benchmark-construction disclosure, additional validation and sensitivity checks, and explicit acknowledgment of image-quality tradeoffs that v2's conclusion glossed over. The central method and headline results remain stable. These gains are limited by new reporting inconsistencies: conflicting seeds, a frequency-ratio formula opposite to its description, and calling N=20 optimal despite lower β at N=5. The added evidence supports a modest overall improvement, not an unqualified strengthening of the conclusions.
